`final class GlfwKeys`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.base.lwjgl3.glfw.input` · **Module:** `base-lwjgl3-glfw` · **Source:** [GlfwKeys.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/base/lwjgl3-glfw/src/main/java/dev/joid/base/lwjgl3/glfw/input/GlfwKeys.java)<br/>
**Backends:** <span class="joid-badge">LWJGL 3</span> <span class="joid-badge">Vulkan</span>

Maps the key codes of GLFW to the keys of JOID and back, by physical position or through the keyboard layout.

## Description

Its position table needs no GLFW call, so a backend whose engine reports GLFW key codes reuses it; `getKey` reads the layout through GLFW.

- [Keys](/build/base-modules/lwjgl3-glfw/#keys)

## Method details

<a id="GlfwKeys-method-getCode"></a>

### getCode

`int getCode(Key key)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the GLFW key code at the physical position of the key, or `GLFW_KEY_UNKNOWN` for a key that GLFW does not name.

<a id="GlfwKeys-method-getKey"></a>

### getKey

`Key getKey(int code)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the key that the code types on the current keyboard layout, read with `glfwGetKeyName`: on an AZERTY keyboard, the code of `Q` gives `Key.A`.

<a id="GlfwKeys-method-getPhysicalKey"></a>

### getPhysicalKey

`Key getPhysicalKey(int code)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the key at the physical position of the code, whatever the layout, or `Key.UNKNOWN`.

<a id="GlfwKeys-method-isKeyDown"></a>

### isKeyDown

`boolean isKeyDown(Key key, IntPredicate down)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

If `true`, the key has a GLFW code and the predicate reports that code as pressed.
